title: One macrostep simulates one source step
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite binary Turing machines, let $a,R\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a binary input word. Suppose the base guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$, its unary tape has a unit marker at $u$, and the data tapes decode to the head-centered payload vectors of $c$. Assume those payload vectors are blank outside $[-R,R]$ for both $c$ and its one-step successor. Then there are new read and neighbor-register vectors and data tapes such that exactly $6R+8$ simulator steps from the macrostep-check phase at unary head $u$, carrying the state and last output bit of $c$, reach the macrostep-check phase at unary head $u+1$, carrying the state and last output bit of the successor configuration, with the new data tapes decoding to that successor's head-centered payload vectors and the output word unchanged.
